summary: This document defines a YANG data model for the delivery of Layer 3 provider-provisioned VPN services. It covers BGP PE-based VPNs and is meant for communication between customers and network operators, instantiated at the operator's management system.

eli5.summary: It is a standard order form a customer can use to request a private network from a provider, so computers on both sides understand the request.

subtitle: A standard order form, written in YANG, for asking a network operator to build a BGP/MPLS Layer 3 VPN.

tldr.problem: Customers and network operators need a common, machine-readable way to describe a Layer 3 VPN service (which sites, which topology, what bandwidth and routing) without exposing router-by-router configuration.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 8299 defines the YANG module ietf-l3vpn-svc with two main containers, vpn-services and sites. A management system takes this abstract service request as input and works out the real device configuration itself.
tldr.outcome: It is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 8049, whose module could not be implemented because of broken XPATH expressions. The new module keeps the same name but is not backward compatible.

today: RFC 8299 is a Proposed Standard that obsoletes RFC 8049. The metadata for this RFC lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: What the Model Is For
sections.content:
RFC 8299 defines a Layer 3 VPN service data model written in YANG. Its elements can be used in communication protocols between customers and network operators, and also as input to automated control and configuration applications.

The scope is deliberately narrow. The model is limited to BGP PE-based VPNs as described in RFC 4026, RFC 4110 and RFC 4364. It is not a configuration model for network elements: it gives an abstracted view of the service, and the management system must use device-specific models to configure the routers. How that is done is out of scope.

The RFC defines a few roles. A Customer Edge (CE) device is equipment dedicated to a customer and connected at Layer 3 to one or more PE devices. A Provider Edge (PE) device is managed by the service provider (SP), can support multiple VPNs for different customers, and is usually at an SP point of presence (POP).
sections.eli5: Think of ordering a pizza by ticking boxes on a form. You do not tell the cook how to knead the dough. This model is the form, and the provider's systems are the cook.

sections.title: Replacing RFC 8049
sections.content:
This document obsoletes RFC 8049 and creates a new module with the same name. The reason was practical: the module in RFC 8049 compiled as YANG but could not be implemented. Several must expressions were broken badly enough that tools which really parse XPATH refused to compile them.

Two further problems were fixed. The English text and the YANG for sorting Access Control List (ACL) rules contradicted each other, and the model used classic ACL rule numbering for something that was semantically ordered-by user. The ACL modeling was also incompatible with other IETF work. Other changes include making the QoS rule id a string instead of a 16-bit integer, using relative instead of absolute paths in some expressions, and adding a check that SLAAC parameters are only used for IPv6.

The RFC argues that keeping the module name is safe. Section 11 of RFC 7950 forbids changes with potential to cause interoperability problems, but because the old module could not be implemented, no client and server could have interoperated using it.
sections.eli5: The first order form had a mistake that made it impossible to fill in. This is the corrected form. Since nobody could use the old one, giving the new one the same name does not confuse anyone.

sections.title: Where the Service Model Sits
sections.content:
The model proposes an abstracted interface between customers and network operators. The operator's system is the server and the customer's system is the client. A typical use is as input to an orchestration layer that translates the request into configuration for the network elements.

Those elements can be routers, but also servers such as AAA. Configuration can be pushed by CLI, by NETCONF or RESTCONF (RFC 6241, RFC 8040) with device YANG models for BGP, VRF, BFD and so on, or by some other technique the operator prefers. The service model can be used by any component of the management system, but not directly by network elements.

Section 8 adds that the management system may be modular, with a service component that instantiates the service model and a configuration component that configures devices. The authors anticipate separate device-level YANG modules for VRF definition, physical interfaces, the IP layer, QoS, routing protocols, multicast VPN and network address translation, and say the list is not exhaustive.
sections.eli5: The customer talks to the provider's front desk, not to the machines in the back room. The front desk turns the request into instructions for each machine.

sections.title: Structure of the YANG Module
sections.content:
The module ietf-l3vpn-svc is divided into two main containers: vpn-services and sites. A vpn-service list entry holds global parameters for one customer's VPN. A site represents a connection of a customer office to one or more VPN services, and is made of at least one site-network-access. A site with several accesses is typically multihomed.

Each site-network-access is attached through a bearer, which covers properties below Layer 3, with an ip-connection on top for Layer 3 properties. A site also carries an availability policy and has a type, point-to-point or multipoint. Parameters such as routing, services and security can be set at both site level and access level; if both are set, the access-level value MUST override the site-level one.

The site-vpn-flavor says how a site is multiplexed across VPNs: site-vpn-flavor-single (one VPN), site-vpn-flavor-multi (all accesses in the same set of VPNs), site-vpn-flavor-sub (each logical access maps to its own VPN or VPNs), and site-vpn-flavor-nni (the site represents an option A network-to-network interface). A site is attached to a VPN through the mandatory vpn-attachment container, either by referencing a vpn-id directly or by referencing a VPN policy for more complex cases.

The model is modular through features such as IPv4, IPv6, extranet VPNs, site diversity and QoS, and can be extended by augmentation.
sections.eli5: A company has offices, and each office has one or more cables to the provider. The model lists the offices, the cables, and which private network each cable joins.

sections.title: VPN Topologies, Cloud Access and Extranets
sections.content:
The VPN service topology is required for configuration. The model supports any-to-any, Hub and Spoke (where Hubs can exchange traffic) and Hub and Spoke disjoint (where Hubs cannot). The default is any-to-any. Each site then has a site-role: in an any-to-any VPN all sites MUST use any-to-any-role, and in the hub topologies they MUST be Hub or Spoke.

Underneath, a PE-based VPN is built from route targets (RTs) as in RFC 4364. The management system is expected to allocate RTs automatically when a VPN is requested, and likewise to allocate a VRF and a route distinguisher on the target PE. How it does so is out of scope. If a suitable VRF already exists on the PE, the site MAY be placed in it.

Other service-level features are cloud access, multicast and extranets. Cloud access uses a cloud-accesses container with an identifier local to each administration; NAT44 is the only address translation option, and by default all sites MUST be authorized to reach the cloud, with permit-site or deny-site leaf-lists to restrict that. For multicast, the model supports bidirectional, shared and source-based customer trees, and requires RP parameters when ASM is requested. The extranet-vpns container lets one VPN reach all resources of another; note that all sites in the other VPN then gain access to all sites in the first.
sections.eli5: Some private clubs let everyone talk to everyone. Others have a head office that every branch talks to, but branches do not talk to each other. The form lets you choose which kind of club you want.

sections.title: Deciding Where to Connect a Site
sections.content:
The management system decides where each site-network-access attaches to the provider network, for example which PE or aggregation switch. It MUST honor all customer constraints. If a constraint is too strict to fulfil, it MUST NOT provision the site and MUST tell the user which constraints failed. Site location and access type are only hints, and the system MAY also use internal criteria such as least load or distance.

For the access type, the bearer container is considered first. requested-type names the media the customer wants, and a strict leaf set to true forbids substitutes. always-on is a strict constraint, and bearer-reference reuses an already-ordered connection and cannot be relaxed.

Access diversity is expressed with group identifiers and constraint types, each stated as: access S must be a given constraint type from these target accesses. A constraint is evaluated against a list of groups, all-other-accesses or all-other-groups. Constraints can conflict, for example one access pe-diverse from another that must be on the same PE. When placement is not possible, the management system MUST return an error saying so.

For availability, the access-priority leaf expresses preference: a higher value is preferred. Equal values model load sharing, different values model primary and backup. The RFC gives A1=100, A2=100, A3=50, A4=50, A5=10 as an example, and admits some scenarios cannot be expressed. A separate traffic-protection setting asks for protection such as local repair, but how it is implemented is out of scope.
sections.eli5: When you ask for two connections, you can say they must not run through the same building, so one flood cannot cut both. If the provider cannot do that, it must tell you rather than guess.

sections.title: Management, Routing and Service Parameters
sections.content:
Three management modes set the responsibility boundary. In provider-managed the CE is managed only by the provider, and the boundary lies between the CE and the customer network. In customer-managed the boundary is between the PE and the CE. In co-managed the provider mainly manages the CE but lets the customer access it, and the boundary is as in provider-managed.

The routing-protocol setting chooses what runs between provider and customer: bgp, rip, ospf, static, direct or vrrp. Dual stack is handled with the address-family leaf-list. Address allocation on the IP connection has five types: provider-dhcp, provider-dhcp-relay, static-address, slaac and provider-dhcp-slaac. If BGP peers use the access connection addresses, static-address MUST be used.

Service parameters include bandwidth, MTU and QoS. Bandwidth is given as svc-input-bandwidth and svc-output-bandwidth in bits per second, from the customer site's point of view. QoS has an ordered qos-classification-policy of rules that match a flow or application and set a target class, and a qos-profile that is either a standard operator profile or a custom list of classes with direction, rate limit, latency, jitter and bandwidth. The management system MUST keep the user's rule order on devices.

For encryption, the layer can be 2 or 3, and a customer profile supports only a pre-shared key. The RFC adds that Carriers' Carriers, and NNIs of options A, B and C from RFC 4364, can be described, and that identifiers such as cloud and QoS profile names are supplied by the SP out of band.
sections.eli5: The form also asks who looks after the equipment, how to share routes, how fast the line should be, and which traffic goes first. Each choice is a tick box.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content:
The module is designed to be accessed through NETCONF or RESTCONF. The mandatory-to-implement secure transport is SSH for NETCONF (RFC 6242) and TLS for RESTCONF (RFC 5246), and the NETCONF access control model (RFC 6536) can restrict users to a subset of operations and content.

Two writable subtrees are called out as sensitive: /l3vpn-svc/vpn-services/vpn-service and /l3vpn-svc/sites/site. They indirectly create or modify PE and CE configuration, so unexpected changes could cause service disruption or network misbehavior. The same subtrees are sensitive to read, because they hold customer-proprietary information such as the customer name, site location and which services are subscribed.

IANA assigned the URI urn:ietf:params:xml:ns:yang:ietf-l3vpn-svc in the IETF XML Registry and recorded the YANG module name ietf-l3vpn-svc with prefix l3vpn-svc. The entries originally assigned for RFC 8049 now refer to this document.
sections.eli5: The order form holds private details about a company, so only trusted people should be allowed to read or change it, and it should travel in a locked envelope.

items.label: Different PE
items.desc: Must not connect to the same PE as the targeted accesses.

items.label: Different POP
items.desc: Must not connect to the same POP as the targeted accesses.

items.label: Different linecard
items.desc: Must not connect to the same linecard as the targeted accesses.

items.label: Different bearer parts
items.desc: Must not share common bearer components, such as a DSLAM, BAS or Layer 2 switch.

items.label: Same PE
items.desc: Must connect to the same PE as the targeted accesses.

items.label: Same bearer
items.desc: Must use the same bearer as the targeted accesses.

items.title: provider-managed
items.text: CE managed only by the provider. Boundary is between the CE and the customer network.

items.title: customer-managed
items.text: CE managed only by the customer. Boundary is between the PE and the CE.

items.title: co-managed
items.text: CE mainly managed by the provider, with customer access for configuration and monitoring. Same boundary as provider-managed.
